A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, core results, and Appendices A–F. All 62 pages of v1 and 71 pages of v2, including figures, equations, and the new appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 presents theoretical results, proofs, and illustrative constructions, but no original empirical outcomes in either the main text or appendices.

after.justification: Section 8 and Appendix I report original OCE benchmark and ablation results. Appendix G.1 additionally measures general-position rates in pretrained and quantized MNIST INRs.

M1.justification: v2 introduces Output Capacity Expansion (OCE), absent from v1: a weight-space network predicts k output networks whose function outputs are averaged. This changes the output representation and inference procedure, and is implemented for DWS and GMN.

E1.justification: v2 adds empirical coverage of MNIST INR image dilation and general-position testing on 60,000 pretrained MNIST INRs under varying quantization precision. v1 discusses applications but does not evaluate these datasets or scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 introduces comparisons with DWS and GMN at k=1, plus NFT, NP-NFN, NG-GNN-64, NG-T-64, ScaleGMN-B, and ScaleGMN + GradMetaNet++. Appendix I.3 distinguishes reproduced DWS/GMN baselines from published scores imported for the other methods. v1 has no empirical comparator set.

E3.justification: New protocols specify MNIST train/test splits with 5,000 validation examples, rendered-image MSE, 150 training epochs, and reduced hidden widths to prevent OCE configurations exceeding baseline parameter budgets. Appendix G.1 adds layerwise quantization and GP-rate measurement procedures.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds an ensemble-size ablation at k=1, 2, 4, and 8 for DWS and GMN under parameter-budget controls. Appendix G.1 adds quantization sensitivity analyses, combined exclusion-set tests, and illustrative digit reconstructions. These empirical analyses are absent from v1.

E5.justification: Appendix I.5 introduces basic uncertainty reporting: three training seeds per configuration and mean and standard deviation of test MSE, displayed for the OCE and ablation results. v1 contains no experimental run-count or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports MSE decreasing from 2.29 to 1.36 for DWS and from 1.96 to 1.06 for GMN as k increases from 1 to 8, in units of 10^-2. Table 1 supports approximately 34% lower MSE than ScaleGMN + GradMetaNet++ at 1.60; Appendix I.6 incorrectly calls that comparator the GMN baseline. Figure 5 newly reports bias-based GP rates falling from 100% unquantized to 0.62% at 8 bits.

T1.justification: The existing MLP results and proofs are largely retained. Appendix G adds p-norm exclusion sets and a canonization approximation proof in Proposition G.3. Appendix H establishes transformer-weight-space GMN universality through Theorem H.2 and Corollary H.3, substantially extending the theoretical scope.

C1.justification: v2 retains the three theoretical contributions but adds a fourth empirical contribution. Its abstract, introduction, and conclusion now claim that OCE translates the theory into practical architectural improvements, including up to 34% lower MSE than prior reported SOTA on INR dilation.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the controlled OCE gains as evidence that output capacity is a practical bottleneck, whereas v1 leaves empirical capacity validation open. Appendix G explains alternatives when biases are absent or shared and interprets quantization-dependent GP failures. The conclusion reframes larger-output architectures as an avenue already partially explored by OCE.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly documents the SIREN architecture, dilation kernel, residual prediction, optimizer settings, learning-rate schedule, and batch size. It specifies A100 hardware, 4–10 hours per run, approximately 200 GPU-hours overall, and a link described as providing code, configurations, and logs. v1 has no corresponding experimental implementation information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is largely retained. Grohe's 2017 book and its citation in the Proposition E.8 proof are removed. v2 additionally positions OCE against already-cited methods using gradients or probes; publication-metadata and citation-style updates do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section order remain intact. v2 revises the abstract, contribution list, and conclusion, inserts an empirical section, and appends G–I. It also standardizes 'cannon' to 'canon' and updates acknowledgements and adds an impact statement, without extensively rewriting the retained exposition.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column presentation, with retained Figures 1–4 resized or relocated. v2 adds two result tables and two quantization figures, including digit reconstructions, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the practical support that v1 explicitly left open: parameter-budget-controlled, three-seed OCE ablations demonstrate an actionable architectural consequence, while Appendix G tests the central GP assumption. The alternative-exclusion-set and transformer results also broaden applicability. Evidence remains confined to MNIST INRs, and Appendix I.6 mislabels the comparator behind the 34% claim, but the tables support the principal empirical conclusion.
